description: Blue (single colour, thin black outlines) figure built only from equilateral triangles on a triangle grid, caption 'Pinwheel'. Centre: a regular hexagon made of 6 triangles meeting at one central point (hexagon corners at the top-left, top-right, right, bottom-right, bottom-left, left; slightly turned, not flat-topped). On each of the 6 sides of the hexagon one rhombus (two triangles joined along an edge) is stuck, so 12 outer triangles in 6 pairs; every rhombus is attached in the same turning sense so the whole figure looks like a six-bladed windmill. A vertical dotted line (grey dashes outside the triangle, black dashes inside) passes through the apex circle, the middle of the triangle and the midpoint of the base, running a little above the top circle and a little below the base. The left half and the right half are mirror halves.

belongs_to: 'What about Figure (b) with the four puzzle pieces and a dotted line passing through the middle? Are they mirror halves? No, when we fold along the line, the left half does not exactly fit over the right half.'
description: Figure (b), caption '(b)' below. Four orange-red jigsaw-puzzle pieces joined in a 2 x 2 block (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right piece), thin dark outlines between pieces, no other colours. Outer knobs (round head on a short neck): the top-left piece has a knob sticking out to the LEFT; the top-right piece has a knob sticking out at the TOP; the bottom-left piece has a knob sticking out at the BOTTOM; the bottom-right piece has a knob sticking out to the RIGHT (4 outer knobs, one on each side of the block, none opposite its mirror position). Outer round bites (holes cut into the edge): the top-left piece on its top edge (right part), the top-right piece on its right edge, the bottom-left piece on its left edge, the bottom-right piece on its bottom edge. Inside, the four pieces interlock through knob-and-hole joints (one joint across each of the four internal edges). A vertical dotted line runs through the middle of the block along the join between the two left pieces and the two right pieces, from above the top to below the bottom. The pieces on the left of the line are NOT mirror images of those on the right (knobs and holes are in different places), so the line is not a line of symmetry.
